15 Bean Soup

Start with a bag of 15 beans or similar varieties.

  • Soak beans overnight. Use plenty of water. If it comes with a seasoning packet, throw it away.
  • Come morning, rinse beans and fill with fresh water.
  • The end goal is a produce that's slightly soupy. You need roughly a couple inches above the beans. Add more water if needed.

Here's where we get into a bit of subjective grey matter. Nothing here is set in stone and must be done using the best judgment of the cook.

You need a bunch of miscellaneous seasoning and spices. My dad manages to accomplish this using only the spice cabinet, kielbasa, and a touch of brown sugar. I'm not that skilled, so I need things like fresh garlic, onions, and bacon.

If bacon, garlic, and onions are used, add them early. If kielbasa is used, it can be added later if desired.

Seasonings should include southwestern and/or smoking stuff. Think cajun, chile peppers, sage, chipotle, maple, applewood, etc. Other things include salt, pepper, bay leaves, parsley, brown sugar, bourbon, etc.

If you can find it, you should add pork bouillon cubes or pork knuckle.

My local big-chain grocer has ≈3lb briskets for usually less than 20 bucks. (Sometimes they're on sale for $12-$15 though, which is when I snatch them up.)

Put one or even two of them in a slow cooker. (One if it's a smaller cooker, I have this one exactly, so it fits two of them nicely.) Add 2/3 to 3/4 of one of these small bottles of McCormick pickling spice per brisket, and fill the cooker with water until everything's covered.

  • Cook on high heat for 2 hrs
  • Then let it go for another 6 on low
  • Shut cooker off, and immediately place brisket(s) into smaller containers using tongs or whatever
  • Use a ladle or scoop of some sort to cover the meat with liquid again
  • Don't completely cover - leave enough for steam to get out
  • Let sit on counter until cool enough to touch
  • Cover completely and put in fridge overnight

Those last steps are the most important. Corned beef has to cool in its liquid, otherwise it ends up dry and chewy. The next day, you'll be amazed at what you have. Slice it thin for sandwiches, slice thick and cube it for hash. Pay attention to the grain of the meat, though - cut it the wrong way and you're still going to be chewing on shoe leather.

Brisket is best, but this recipe also works nicely on eye of round - you can get a half of one at 4-6lbs, or a whole one at 6-8lbs.

CTHULHU'S ATOMIC CHILI

Ingredients:

  • 1-1.5 pounds or so of ground meat, your choice
  • 3 big cans (28 oz. or so) of tomatoes (I usually use 2 crushed and 1 puree)
  • 1 large red onion
  • 2 large bell peppers of any color
  • An assortment of hot peppers to taste
  • 3 cans of beans, your choice (I usually use black, dark red kidney, and pinto)
  • 4+ cloves fresh garlic
  • Spices as detailed below

Instructions:

  • Add tomatoes to crockpot and turn on 'high'.
  • In your cast-iron skillet, brown meat almost all the way through. Add to crockpot and stir to mix.
  • Chop onion add to pot, and stir to mix.
  • Drain slime from beans, rinse in colander, add to pot, and stir to mix.
  • Chop peppers, add to pot, and stir to mix.
  • Finely chop garlic, add to pot, and stir to taste.

  • Add spices to taste. The exact blend will depend on your choice of meat. I usually use cumin, smoked chipotle powder, cayenne (not necessary if you've used fresh hot peppers), and a little dash of maple syrup.

  • Heat, covered, on 'high' setting, until the mixture reaches criticality (i.e., it starts simmering).

  • Reduce heat to 'low' and simmer at criticality, stirring about once an hour or so. The chili must remain at criticality for at least two hours. Four hours is better. Six hours is even better.
  • Serve with full-fat Greek yogurt and corn bread.

Makes enough to feed a crowd, or dinner for two plus a week's worth of lunches. Total cost ~$20.
